reason: A common misspelling of exserted (projecting beyond the enclosing structure); the opposite of FLOPO:0991121 included.

target: cystolith present (no PO class: a cystolith part class is needed in FLOPO, under or part of idioblast PO_0000283)
reason: 'With cystoliths' says a part is present, as with lenticellate. PO has no cystolith (a calcium carbonate body inside a lithocyst idioblast), so the rule needs that bearer class first.
'Stems not rooting at the nodes' means no adventitious roots form on the shoot; PO_0000042 has adventitious root as a synonym. 'At the nodes' and 'at the apex' stay as region context.
Articulate pedicels, leaflets and pinnae are jointed (with a joint where they separate); this negates FLOPO:0991154 jointed.
'Sub-' on a shape word is the approximate-value pattern, as with suborbicular. PATO's definition of obtuse is weak; if an 'obtuse (sensu botany)' class is made, as for acute, it should be the value.

label: tailed
definition: A caudate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a slender, tail-like appendage at one or both ends, as at the base of an anther or the end of a seed.
reason: PATO:0001880 caudate is defined loosely (any tail-like projection) and its only synonym, 'caudal', is positional. A botanical child makes the seed and anther sense explicit; if curators judge PATO:0001880 enough, map to it directly.
'Extending to the costa' or 'to the tooth tip' is relational and names the second part; the relation is PATO_0002463 extends to. Without a second term it should be dropped.
Barren florets and spikelets bear no functional sexual organs or grain: PATO_0000956 sterile.
Emersed leaves and inflorescences rise above the surface of the water: FLOPO emergent, the counterpart of submerged and floating.
A carrot-shaped root, caudex or fruit is an elongated cone tapering to the tip: PATO conical. It is not fusiform, which tapers at both ends.

target: new: compound of two qualities of one bearer (conjunction): finely toothed, dentated PATO_0001205, with the teeth gland-tipped
reason: The word joins two statements about one margin: it has small teeth, and the teeth end in glands. It is a conjunction, not a single quality and not a continuum.
A count of ovules per locule or ovary, like 'few-flowered'.

label: semi-ovate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being that of one half of an ovate figure divided lengthwise, one margin nearly straight and the other curved, broadest below the middle.
reason: A standard term for the asymmetric outline of orchid lateral sepals and fern pinna halves; no PATO or FLOPO term covers half of a shape. It should go under FLOPO:0991024 ovate once that temporary class is replaced.

label: hemiepiphytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing as an epiphyte for part of its life and rooted in the ground for the other part, either starting on a host and later sending roots to the ground or starting in the ground and later losing its connection to it.
reason: A distinct life form, a sibling of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic and FLOPO:0991111 terrestrial; mapping to epiphytic would be wrong. Probably outside PATO's scope, as for epiphytic.
The same as rule C316 for 'thread-like': PATO filiform.
Flabelliform means fan-shaped, as rule C227 for flabellate.
A count of ovules (exactly one) per locule, carpel or ovary.

target: new: growth form of the whole plant (tree habit), with decreased height PATO_0000569
reason: A habit noun (a small tree) with no PATO or FLOPO value; it should be handled with tree, shrub and the other growth forms, not as a single word.
Shredding bark peels in long strips, which is covered by FLOPO exfoliating. Leaf tips that shred into fibres are a different sense and stay out of this rule.
Conoid means cone-shaped: PATO conical (synonym cone-shaped).
Not a quality word: it is a measurement of the filament. The bearer should be filament (PO_0009067), not stamen, with the number as a bounded measurement.

label: biserrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing large forward-pointing teeth that themselves bear smaller forward-pointing teeth.
reason: A standard margin type that PATO lacks; it is a serrated margin with teeth of two sizes.
PATO elliptic has ellipsoid as a synonym. 'Narrowly' is a degree word that narrows the value; keep it as a cue in the record rather than making a new class.
Glandular punctate leaves and calyces are marked with dots that are glands: FLOPO gland-dotted.
Thick-textured leaves, bracts or petals have a thick, firm substance; the firm content is increased thickness.

Not a quality word: it is a length (PATO_0000122) of the tube of the named organ. PO has no corolla, calyx or stamen tube class, and 'tube' alone was rejected as a generic part; this needs the bounded-measurement pattern on a part of the named organ.
'Narrowed' maps to PATO tapered (rule C172), so 'not narrowed' negates it. Where the cue names a region ('at the base'), that stays as region context.
The same as rule C315 for cushion-shaped: PATO pulvinate.
'Expanded' maps to PATO dilated (rule C181), so 'not expanded' negates it.
